topics.label: Course welcome and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This opening section introduces the lecturer, outlines the scope of the lecture series on cancer causation, and presents the core learning outcomes.

topics.label: Foundations of cancer etiology: genetics, environment, and stochastic risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the fundamental drivers of cancer development, examining how endogenous biological processes, inherited genetics, environmental exposures, and stochastic risk contribute to malignancy and geographic variations in incidence.

topics.label: Specific carcinogenic agents, chemical mechanisms, and tumor promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail specific biological, physical, and chemical carcinogens, explaining their molecular mechanisms of DNA damage, metabolic activation, tumor promotion through chronic inflammation, and tissue-specific vulnerabilities.

topics.label: Methods for detecting carcinogenicity and evaluating cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro methodologies used to identify carcinogens and prove their causal link to cancer, concluding with risk-benefit considerations.
